note_on_method: Every court count and every surface below comes from that park's own page on cityofmadison.com, in the block the City heads "Tennis & Pickleball" or, at Garner Park, "Pickleball". Every address comes from the City's pickleball courts list. Where a park page says nothing about its courts beyond that block, and several say very little about the park at all, this page says nothing either. Nobody working on this has played on these courts.

slots.description: Two courts on asphalt, on a 6.47-acre neighbourhood park on Madison's west side. The City describes Bordner as "the perfect location for nearby residents, families, and people of all ages", with basketball courts, an open field for a pick-up game of soccer, a playground, and the tennis courts that carry the pickleball lines. That last detail is the one to hold on to: like nineteen of Madison's twenty outdoor pickleball venues, this is a tennis court with pickleball markings on it rather than a pickleball court.
slots.getting_there: 5610 Elder Pl., Madison, WI 53705, which the Census geocoder matched cleanly to Madison city, Dane County. The City publishes nothing about parking at any of its pickleball venues, and on a park of this size (under seven acres, in a residential street grid) the realistic expectation is street parking rather than a lot. Nothing on the park page confirms it either way.
slots.what_to_expect: Two courts, shared with tennis, played over a tennis net Madison notes is about two inches taller than a standard pickleball net. Individuals play first come, first served; leagues and lessons must reserve in advance, and the City does not publish where those bookings appear. Lighting is not stated here, so plan for daylight. With two courts and a neighbourhood catchment, this is a venue for a pair or two rather than a group. No restrooms, shelter, parking or hours are published for Bordner.

faqs.a: Two, on asphalt. The City states it in one line on the park's own page, under the heading "Tennis & Pickleball": "Courts: 2, asphalt".
No. They are tennis courts striped for pickleball, which is how nineteen of Madison's twenty outdoor venues work. Garner Park has the city's only dedicated outdoor pickleball courts.
Not stated. Only Tenney Park's courts are marked lighted on Madison's pickleball list; every other venue including this one is unknown rather than confirmed dark.

slots.description: Four courts on asphalt, the largest shared-court count in Madison, on a 25.81-acre park stretching along Monona Bay just west of downtown. The City's page lists the Jenni and Kyle Foundation Accessible Playground, a reservable shelter, multipurpose fields, a nature nook, a beach house with Madison Boats running watercraft rentals, an off-leash dog park and a sand volleyball court. After three larger pickleball sites in the city fell out of this directory on address checks, Brittingham's four courts are the second-largest count published in Madison, behind Garner's six.
slots.getting_there: 388 S. Bassett St., Madison, WI 53703, and that address is worth reading carefully, because it is not the park's. The City lists Brittingham's main entrance at 829 W. Washington Ave. and prints the courts separately at S. Bassett St., a different street on a park that runs along a bay. If you navigate to the park's headline address you will be at the playground and shelters, not the courts.
slots.what_to_expect: Four tennis courts striped for pickleball, played over a tennis net about two inches higher than a pickleball net, first come first served for individuals. The park page carries a note the City has left standing since the courts reopened: "Update November 5, 2025: Fencing work is nearly complete and courts are open again!" Lighting is not stated. Four courts is enough for a group of eight to rotate, which is not true of most Madison venues. The courts sit on the Bassett Street side, so the beach, the boats and the dog park are a walk away rather than beside you.

faqs.a: Four, on asphalt: "Tennis & Pickleball / 388 S. Bassett St. / Courts: 4, asphalt" on the park's own page. That is the largest shared-court count published in Madison.
They were. The City's page carries an update dated 5 November 2025 saying fencing work was nearly complete and the courts were open again. Nothing on the page reports a current closure.

slots.description: Three courts on asphalt in the largest community park Madison Parks runs, 250.82 acres in the south-west corner of the city. The City's own summary gives the scale: "The largest community park in Madison Parks, Elver Park spans an impressive 250 acres in the southwest corner of the city. Elver features two reservable shelters, a splash park, athletic fields, a disc golf course and more." The pickleball is three courts of that, striped onto tennis courts.
slots.getting_there: 1250 McKenna Blvd., Madison, WI 53719, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. On a 250-acre park the address is the entrance rather than the court, and the City publishes no guidance on where within the park to head or where to leave a car. Budget time to find them.
slots.what_to_expect: Three courts shared with tennis, on asphalt, played over a tennis net at tennis height. First come, first served for individuals; leagues and lessons reserve in advance. Three is an awkward number for rotation but a good one for arriving in a group of four with a spare. Lighting is not stated. The City publishes no map reference for where in 250 acres the courts sit, and no restroom or parking information for them. On a park this size that is a real gap.

faqs.a: Three, on asphalt, stated on Elver Park's page as "Tennis & Pickleball / Courts: 3, asphalt".

faqs.q: Can I book a court here?
faqs.a: Not as an individual. Madison's outdoor courts are first come, first served; only leagues and lessons reserve. The one bookable pickleball venue in the city is indoors, at the Warner Park Community Recreation Center.

faqs.q: Are there restrooms at the courts?
faqs.a: Not stated. On a 250-acre park with shelters and a splash park there are facilities somewhere, but the City does not say where they are relative to the courts.

slots.description: Six dedicated pickleball courts on asphalt: the only dedicated outdoor pickleball courts in Madison, and the city's first. The City states both facts itself. Its pickleball page says "Garner Park offers Madison's only dedicated outdoor pickleball courts", and the park's own page dates them: "Madison's first dedicated pickleball courts, located in Garner Park, opened in 2016." Everything else outdoors in this city is a tennis court with lines added. Garner is 41.83 acres on the west side, most of it rising along a knoll to an overlook where the award-winning park shelter sits, and it is the home of Opera in the Park.
slots.getting_there: 333 S. Rosa Rd., Madison, WI 53705, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. The park's shelter is reservable for picnics and gatherings, which implies vehicle access, but the City publishes nothing about parking here or at any other Madison pickleball venue. Note the park is on a knoll: the courts and the overlook are not at the same elevation.
slots.what_to_expect: The only place in Madison where you are playing on a pickleball court rather than a tennis court: a proper net at the proper height, no tennis lines to read through, and six courts, which is enough for a genuine rotation. Individuals play first come, first served; leagues and lessons must reserve in advance, and with six dedicated courts this is the likeliest venue in the city to have one of those running. Neither lighting nor whether nets are provided is stated. On a summer evening, note that Opera in the Park draws crowds to this park specifically.

faqs.a: Yes, and the City says so twice. Its pickleball page states that "Garner Park offers Madison's only dedicated outdoor pickleball courts", and the park page records them as Madison's first, opened in 2016.

Because a dual-striped court uses a tennis net, which Madison notes is about two inches taller than a standard pickleball net. At Garner the net is the right height and the lines are the only lines. Nineteen of the city's twenty outdoor venues are the other kind.
Not stated. Even Madison's flagship pickleball site carries no lighting statement; only Tenney Park's line ends in "lighted".

slots.description: Two courts on asphalt at an 8.11-acre park on Madison's east side, which the City describes as "a beautiful park on Madison's east side, near Kennedy Elementary School and adjacent to Heritage Sanctuary". The sanctuary is the distinguishing feature: this is a neighbourhood park backing onto conservation land rather than a sports site, and the pickleball is two tennis courts carrying pickleball lines, the most common arrangement in the city.
slots.getting_there: 701 Meadowlark Dr., Madison, WI 53714, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. The City publishes nothing about parking here. On an eight-acre park in a residential street grid, the realistic expectation is street parking.
slots.what_to_expect: Two shared courts, first come first served, over a tennis net about two inches too high for pickleball. No lighting is stated, so plan for daylight. On an eight-acre neighbourhood park adjacent to a conservation area there is nowhere to wait but courtside, which makes this a venue for one group rather than several. The City publishes no restrooms, parking, shelter or hours for this park, so the record here is the count, the surface, the acreage, the address and the two landmarks it names.

faqs.a: Two, on asphalt: "Tennis & Pickleball / Courts: 2, asphalt" on the park's page.

faqs.q: Is there a nearby alternative if the courts are busy?
faqs.a: Kennedy Park, also two courts on asphalt, is the closest published venue on the same side of the city. Beyond that, Olbrich Park has two and Tenney three.
Not stated. The City's page for this park does not list them, which means it has not said rather than that there are none.

slots.description: Two courts on asphalt at a 13-acre park on Madison's south-west side. The City notes that Huegel is "jointly developed and maintained by the City of Madison" together with a partner body, a shared-stewardship arrangement that does not change who publishes the court count: the Parks Division does, in the same structured line as everywhere else. Two tennis courts, striped for pickleball, on asphalt.
slots.getting_there: 5902 Williamsburg Way, Madison, WI 53719, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. Westhaven Trails Park, also two courts, is the nearest published alternative on the same side of the city, and Elver Park's three are a short distance further south-west.
slots.what_to_expect: Two shared courts, first come first served for individuals, played over a tennis net Madison notes is about two inches taller than a pickleball net. Lighting is not stated. This is a neighbourhood park rather than a destination, so the realistic expectation is a quiet court on a weekday and a queue of one on a weekend evening, though the City publishes no demand figures anywhere and that sentence is inference rather than fact. Nothing is published about restrooms, parking or hours here.

faqs.a: The City of Madison Parks Division publishes and maintains the record, and describes the park as jointly developed and maintained with a partner. The court count and surface here are the City's own.
Asphalt, which is what eighteen of Madison's twenty outdoor pickleball venues are. The City states the material but publishes nothing about its condition: no resurfacing dates, no crack notes.

faqs.q: Where else can I play on this side of the city?
faqs.a: Westhaven Trails Park has two courts and Elver Park three, both in the south-west. Those three sites are the whole of the published inventory for this corner of Madison.

slots.description: Two courts on asphalt at a 22.72-acre east-side park that the City describes as "a popular location for youth soccer leagues and neighborhood children playing on the play equipment or riding their bikes on the trail going through the park and to Kennedy Elementary School". That is a fair warning about the character of the place on a Saturday morning: the pickleball is two tennis courts striped for the sport, on a site whose main business is youth sport and a school route.
slots.getting_there: 5202 Retana Dr., Madison, WI 53714, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. The park has a trail running through it and on to Kennedy Elementary School, which the City mentions, so arriving on foot or by bike from the surrounding neighbourhood is a normal way to get here. Nothing is published about parking.
slots.what_to_expect: Two shared courts, first come first served, tennis net at tennis height. Lighting is not stated. The soccer leagues the City names do not compete for the courts, but they compete for the park, so expect the site to be busy in youth-sport season even when the courts are free. Heritage Heights Park, also two courts, is the nearest published alternative if they are not.

faqs.a: Two, on asphalt: "Tennis & Pickleball / Courts: 2, asphalt".

faqs.q: Are the courts shared with tennis?
faqs.a: Yes, like nineteen of Madison's twenty outdoor venues. You play over the tennis net, which Madison notes is about two inches taller than a pickleball net.
Not stated. The City's page for this park does not list them.

slots.description: One court on asphalt, the smallest pickleball venue in Madison, at a 5.21-acre park on the near west side. The City's page focuses on an arrangement rather than the sport: the playground between Thoreau Elementary School and Nakoma Park is jointly used under an agreement between the City and the school district. The pickleball is a single court striped onto the park's tennis court, which means that when someone is playing tennis, there is no pickleball here at all.
slots.getting_there: 3801 Cherokee Dr., Madison, WI 53711, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. It is a residential pocket of the near west side, adjacent to an elementary school, and the City publishes nothing about parking. On a five-acre neighbourhood park beside a school, treat that as street parking and expect school-run traffic at the obvious hours.
slots.what_to_expect: One court, shared with tennis, over a tennis net about two inches taller than a pickleball net. That is the whole venue. It is fine for a single game of doubles by arrangement and unsuitable for a group, and if the tennis court is in use there is no second court to fall back on. Norman Clayton Park and Westmorland Park, each with two, are the nearest published alternatives on this side of the city. No restrooms, parking, lighting or hours are published for Nakoma.

faqs.a: One, on asphalt: "Tennis & Pickleball / Courts: 1, asphalt". It is the only single-court venue published in Madison.

faqs.q: What happens if someone is playing tennis?
faqs.a: Then the court is taken. With one court and no dedicated pickleball surface, tennis and pickleball cannot both happen here, which is the practical reason a single-court overlay venue is worth reading carefully rather than counting as "has pickleball".
Not stated, like every Madison venue except Tenney Park. On a single court with no lighting statement, daylight is the safe assumption.

slots.description: Two courts on asphalt at one of the smallest parks in this set: 3.44 acres on Madison's west side. The City's page is unusually sparse about the park itself. What it does record is a second way in, noting access at "6402 Piping Rock Road, also path between 6410 & 6502 Piping Rock Road", which is the kind of detail that matters at a pocket park where the obvious frontage may not be the one nearest the courts. The pickleball is two tennis courts carrying pickleball lines.
slots.getting_there: 6401 Shoreham Dr., Madison, WI 53711 is the address the City lists for the courts, and the Census geocoder matched it to Madison city, Dane County. The park page also names access from Piping Rock Road, including a path between two house numbers, so on a 3.44-acre site it is worth knowing which side you are approaching from. No parking guidance is published.
slots.what_to_expect: Two shared courts, first come first served, tennis net at tennis height, no lighting on record. On three and a half acres there is very little else here. The City lists no shelter, no restroom and no other courts, so this is a venue you go to in order to play rather than to spend an afternoon. Nakoma Park is a mile or so away with a single court; Westmorland Park has two on tile. No hours or parking guidance is published either.

faqs.a: Two, on asphalt: "Tennis & Pickleball / Courts: 2, asphalt" on the park's own page.
3.44 acres, the smallest park published in Madison, smaller than Reynolds Park's 3.58 and Waunona's 5.13.
If you live nearby, yes. If you are crossing the city, Garner Park's six dedicated courts or Brittingham Park's four give a group somewhere to rotate, which two courts on three acres does not.

slots.description:
Two courts on asphalt at a 10.3-acre park on Madison's north side. This is one of the venues where the City's record is a court count and very little else: the park page carries the structured "Tennis & Pickleball / Courts: 2, asphalt" block and no descriptive text about the park at all.

The north side is also where Madison's only indoor courts are: five at the Warner Park Community Recreation Center, about a mile and a half away, which are among the few bookable pickleball courts in this directory.
slots.getting_there: 902 Northland Dr., Madison, WI 53704, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. Warner Park, with three outdoor courts and the city's only indoor ones at the recreation center, is the nearest larger site on the same side of the city.
slots.what_to_expect: Two shared courts, first come first served, over a tennis net that Madison notes is about two inches taller than a standard pickleball net. Lighting is not stated. Beyond that, the honest answer is that nobody has published one: the City's page lists no restrooms, no shelter, no parking, no playground and no hours. It records 10.3 acres and two asphalt courts, and everything else about this venue is unpublished.

faqs.a: Two, on asphalt, from the structured block on the park's own page: "Tennis & Pickleball / Courts: 2, asphalt".

faqs.q: Is the park worth visiting for anything else?
faqs.a: We cannot say. The City publishes no description or amenity list for it, and this directory does not describe parks it has only read a court count for.

The Warner Park Community Recreation Center, on the same side of the city, has five indoor courts, among the few bookable pickleball courts in this directory. It requires an active WPCRC ID and either a membership or a daily admission.

slots.description: Two courts on asphalt at a 90-acre park on the shore of Lake Monona, adjacent to the Olbrich Botanical Gardens. The City's own description calls it a place for "a day of leisure, a picnic with your family, or just a great place to revitalize". It is one of the more attractive settings for a pickleball court in this directory and one of the smaller counts on a park of that size: two courts on 90 acres, striped onto tennis courts.
slots.getting_there: 3527 Atwood Ave., Madison, WI 53714, on the east side along the lake shore, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. The botanical gardens next door draw their own visitors, so the area is busier than the court count suggests. As everywhere in Madison, no parking guidance is published for the courts themselves.
slots.what_to_expect: Two shared courts, first come first served, tennis net at tennis height, no lighting on record. The setting is the reason to come, Lake Monona on one side and the botanical gardens on the other, rather than the facilities, and with only two courts a group of eight will be waiting. Tenney Park, three courts and the only lit venue in the city, is the nearest larger alternative on this side of town. No restrooms or parking is published for the courts themselves.

faqs.a: Two, on asphalt: "Tennis & Pickleball / Courts: 2, asphalt" on the park's own page.

faqs.q: Didn't this park have four courts?
faqs.a: The imported record this directory started from said four. The City of Madison's own page says two, so two is what we publish. An operator beats an unsourced dataset every time, and the change is logged in the conflicts report for this city.
Not stated. Only Tenney Park's courts are marked lighted anywhere on Madison's pickleball list.

slots.description: Two courts on "sport court tile", one of only two venues in Madison whose surface is not asphalt or concrete. Reynolds is a 3.58-acre park on the near east side, a few blocks from the Capitol, and the surface is the reason to know about it: modular tile is laid in panels over a base rather than poured, and it plays faster and drains differently from asphalt. Madison states it in the same line as the count.
slots.getting_there: 810 E. Mifflin St., Madison, WI 53703, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. This is dense near-east-side street grid a short distance from the Capitol square, so the practical expectation is on-street parking; the City publishes no guidance. Tenney Park, three lit courts, is the nearest other venue on this side of the isthmus.
slots.what_to_expect: Two courts on tile, shared with tennis, played over a tennis net that Madison notes is about two inches taller than a pickleball net. First come, first served for individuals. Lighting is not stated. On a 3.58-acre park in a dense neighbourhood there is little space to wait, so this is a venue for a pair or two. Nothing is published about restrooms, parking or hours at Reynolds.

faqs.q: What are the courts made of?
faqs.a: "Sport court tile", in the City's words, recorded here under the controlled value modular_tile. Reynolds and Westmorland are the only two Madison venues that are not asphalt.

faqs.q: Does the surface actually play differently?
faqs.a: Modular tile is laid in panels over a base rather than poured flat, and it drains and rebounds differently from asphalt. The City states the material and says nothing about how it plays or what condition it is in, so that is as far as the record goes.

faqs.q: Where is the other tile court?
faqs.a: Westmorland Park, on the near west side at 4114 Tokay Blvd. Those two venues are the only non-asphalt outdoor surfaces published in Madison.

slots.description: Two courts on asphalt at a 10.25-acre park on Madison's far east side. Like several parks in this set, the City's page carries the structured court block, "Tennis & Pickleball / Courts: 2, asphalt", without a description of the park itself, so what we can source here is the count, the surface, the address and the county, and not much else. Two tennis courts striped for pickleball is the standard Madison arrangement, and this is a standard example of it.
slots.getting_there: 6117 Cottontail Trl., Madison, WI 53718, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County, one of the eastern-most published venues in the city. Nothing is published about parking. Heritage Heights Park and Kennedy Park, each two courts, are the nearest published alternatives heading back towards the centre.
slots.what_to_expect: Two shared courts, first come first served, tennis net at tennis height, lighting not stated. The City publishes no restrooms, shelter or amenities for this park, which means it has not said rather than that there are none. Treat it as a neighbourhood court: fine for a game arranged in advance with three friends, not a venue to bring a group to on spec.

faqs.q: What else is in the park?
faqs.a: Not stated. The City's page for Richmond Hill carries the court information and no park description or amenity list, so we publish neither.
Yes. The block is headed "Tennis & Pickleball", which in Madison means tennis courts striped for pickleball, so you play over the tennis net.
Not stated. Tenney Park is the only Madison venue with a lighting statement.

slots.description: Three courts on asphalt, and the only outdoor venue in Madison the City marks as lit: the line on the park's page reads "Courts: 3, asphalt, lighted". Tenney is 38.12 acres on the near east side along the Yahara River, and the City's description is unusually lyrical for a parks page: "With its friendly atmosphere and impressive display of storybook scenery Tenney Park serves as a place to socialize, a peaceful recluse, and a place to just be. It's an excellent place to watch boats launch, seagulls flock, let the children play at the park, or just catch up on some reading."
slots.getting_there: 1414 E. Johnson St., Madison, WI 53703, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. The park sits on the isthmus between Lake Mendota and the Yahara River locks, a short distance from the Capitol, so it is reachable on foot and by bike from much of the near east side. The City publishes nothing about parking here or anywhere else in its pickleball listings.
slots.what_to_expect: Three courts shared with tennis, played over a tennis net about two inches taller than a pickleball net, first come first served. The difference from every other outdoor court in this city is the lights, and the City marks lighting at the level of the whole court block, so all three courts are covered by that one word. Nothing is published about restrooms or parking at the courts.

faqs.a: Yes, and Tenney is the only Madison venue where we can say so. The City's line reads "Courts: 3, asphalt, lighted", and no other park's does. Madison marks the lit courts rather than the unlit ones, so everywhere else is unknown rather than dark.
Not published. The City states that the courts are lit and says nothing about hours, so we cannot tell you when the lights go off.

faqs.q: Are the courts shared with tennis?
faqs.a: Yes. Even Madison's only lit pickleball is on tennis courts striped for the sport, so you are playing over a tennis net about two inches taller than a pickleball net.

slots.description: Two courts on asphalt at a 20.25-acre west-side park that the City describes as "a popular place for families in the neighborhood to play", with "expansive play equipment, soccer fields and lots of open space to spark your imagination". The pickleball is the usual Madison arrangement, two tennis courts carrying pickleball lines, on a park whose main draw is clearly the playground and the open ground rather than the courts.
slots.getting_there: 202 N. Westfield Rd., Madison, WI 53717, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. Nothing is published about parking; on a twenty-acre west-side park the realistic expectation is a street space or a lot the City does not describe.
slots.what_to_expect: Two shared courts, first come first served for individuals, over a tennis net at tennis height. Lighting is not stated. With family use of the playground and soccer fields alongside, expect the park to be busy at weekends without that telling you anything definite about the courts themselves. No restrooms, parking or hours are published for this park.

faqs.a: Two, on asphalt: "Tennis & Pickleball / Courts: 2, asphalt".

faqs.q: What if the courts are busy?
faqs.a: Wexford Park is on the same road, at 1201 N. Westfield Rd., with two more courts on asphalt. They are the closest pair of published venues in the city.
The City describes expansive play equipment, soccer fields and open space, so the park is set up for families. It says nothing about junior pickleball specifically.
Not stated. Only Tenney Park's courts are marked lighted in Madison.

slots.description:
Three outdoor courts on asphalt at a 213-acre park on Madison's north side, which the City calls "distinctive for its natural beauty and expansive tracts of land". The Warner Park Community Recreation Center stands in this park at the same street address and holds five indoor courts, published here as a separate venue because the City runs it as a separate facility with its own membership, ID card and booking system.

Three outdoor courts is mid-table for Madison, level with Elver and Tenney. What is not mid-table is the site: 213 acres, the second-largest park published here, and the only address in the city with both outdoor and indoor pickleball on it. Across this whole directory only eight other places manage that, and at each of them the operator ran both as one facility, so one venue was published. Madison runs them as two, so there are two pages.
slots.getting_there: 2930 N. Sherman Ave., Madison, WI 53704, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. The recreation center shares that address, so if you are meeting someone, say whether you mean the outdoor courts or the gyms. They are different entrances to different things, and only one of them can be booked.
slots.what_to_expect: Three courts shared with tennis, on asphalt, first come first served, played over a tennis net about two inches taller than a pickleball net. Lighting is not stated outdoors. The genuine advantage here is the fallback: if the weather turns or the courts are taken, the recreation center in the same park has five indoor courts, though you will need a WPCRC ID and either a membership or a daily admission to use them. Nothing is published about restrooms or parking at the outdoor courts.

faqs.q: Can I book the outdoor courts?
faqs.a: No. Only the recreation center's five indoor courts take bookings; the three outdoor ones are first come, first served for individuals, with leagues and lessons reserving in advance.
Asphalt outdoors. The gym floors at the recreation center are not described anywhere the City publishes, so that venue reads "not stated" on surface.
Not stated. Tenney Park is the only Madison venue whose courts the City marks as lighted.

slots.description: Two courts on asphalt at a 5.13-acre park on Madison's south side, near the Lake Monona shore. The City's page is brief and its one notable line is a rule rather than a description: "Alcohol is prohibited in this park." That is worth publishing because it is specific, checkable and the kind of thing a group organising an evening game would want to know in advance. The pickleball itself is the standard Madison arrangement: two tennis courts striped for the sport.
slots.getting_there: 5323 Raywood Rd., Madison, WI 53713, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. This is a residential pocket on the south side; the City publishes no parking guidance, and on a five-acre park the realistic expectation is the street.
slots.what_to_expect: Two shared courts, first come first served, tennis net at tennis height, lighting not stated. Alcohol is prohibited in the park, which the City states outright. Beyond that the record is thin: no restrooms, shelter, parking, hours or amenity list are published for Waunona. The court block and the acreage are the substance of the record.

faqs.a: Two, on asphalt: "Tennis & Pickleball / Courts: 2, asphalt".
Not alcohol. The City states plainly that "Alcohol is prohibited in this park", which is one of very few venue-specific rules published anywhere in Madison's pickleball listings.
5.13 acres, which makes it one of the smaller published venues in the city, alongside Nakoma at 5.21 and Westhaven Trails at 5.55.
Not stated. Tenney Park is the only Madison venue whose courts the City marks as lighted.

slots.description: Two courts on asphalt at a 5.55-acre park on Madison's south-west side. The City gives a full amenity sentence for this one: "This southwest side park features a reservable picnic shelter, playground, ballfield, tennis courts, basketball court, and an open field with soccer goals." The tennis courts in that list are the pickleball courts, two of them, striped, which is the arrangement at nineteen of the city's twenty outdoor venues.
slots.getting_there: 3020 Cimarron Trl., Madison, WI 53719, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. Huegel Park, also two courts, is the nearest published venue on the same side of the city, and Elver Park's three are a short distance away. For this corner of Madison, those three sites are the whole of the published inventory.
slots.what_to_expect: Two shared courts, first come first served, over a tennis net about two inches too high for pickleball. Lighting is not stated. The picnic shelter is reservable, which is a real advantage if you are organising a group session and want somewhere to sit between games, though the shelter is bookable and the courts are not. No restrooms, parking or hours are published for the park.

faqs.a: The picnic shelter, yes: the City lists it as reservable. The courts, no. Outdoor pickleball courts in Madison are first come, first served for individuals, and only leagues and lessons reserve.

faqs.q: What else is in the park?
faqs.a: A playground, a ballfield, a basketball court and an open field with soccer goals, alongside the tennis courts that carry the pickleball lines.
Not stated. Tenney Park is the only Madison venue with a lighting statement.

slots.description: Two courts on "sport court tile", one of only two non-asphalt surfaces in Madison. Westmorland is 11.69 acres on the near west side, and the City's description is one of the fuller ones: "Westmorland Park features a rock garden, basketball court, large playground, volleyball court, tennis courts and softball field." The tennis courts there are the pickleball courts, and the tile underfoot is what distinguishes them from eighteen other Madison venues.
slots.getting_there: 4114 Tokay Blvd., Madison, WI 53711, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. It is a settled near-west-side neighbourhood; the City publishes no parking guidance. Nakoma Park, with the city's only single court, is the nearest other published venue, and Norman Clayton Park's two are also close by.
slots.what_to_expect: Two courts on modular tile, shared with tennis, played over a tennis net Madison notes is about two inches taller than a pickleball net. First come, first served. Lighting is not stated. If you have only ever played on asphalt, this and Reynolds Park are the two places in the city to find out what tile feels like. The shelter with its working fireplace is reservable from April to October, which makes this a plausible venue for an organised group in shoulder season. No restrooms, parking or hours are published for the courts.

faqs.q: What are the courts made of?
faqs.a: "Sport court tile" in the City's words, recorded here as modular_tile. Only Reynolds Park shares that surface in Madison; the other eighteen outdoor venues are asphalt.

faqs.q: What else is in the park?
faqs.a: A rock garden, a basketball court, a large playground, a volleyball court and a softball field on 11.69 acres.

faqs.q: Where is the other tile court?
faqs.a: Reynolds Park, at 810 E. Mifflin St. on the near east side. Those two are the only non-asphalt pickleball surfaces published in Madison.

slots.description: Two courts on asphalt at a 20.6-acre west-side park, which the City describes as featuring "a shelter, adjacent woods, and unique playground equipment", popular for youth soccer and for ice skating in winter, with "extensive flower gardens maintained by neighborhood volunteers". The pickleball is two tennis courts carrying pickleball lines. The ice skating is worth noting for what it implies about the season: this is a park that changes use in winter, and no lighting is stated at the courts.
slots.getting_there: 1201 N. Westfield Rd., Madison, WI 53717, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. Walnut Grove Park is on the same road at number 202 with two more courts, the two closest published pickleball venues in Madison, so this corner of the west side has four courts between two parks a short drive apart.
slots.what_to_expect: Two shared courts, first come first served, tennis net at tennis height, no lighting on record. In a Wisconsin winter that combination means daylight only, on asphalt, at a park the City itself associates with skating rather than racket sport. The volunteer-maintained flower gardens and the adjacent woods make it a pleasant place to be in summer; the realistic read is a quiet neighbourhood venue for a pair or two. Nothing is published about restrooms, parking or hours here.

faqs.q: What is the park known for?
faqs.a: The City names youth soccer, winter ice skating, a shelter, adjacent woods, unique playground equipment and extensive flower gardens maintained by neighbourhood volunteers.

Nothing is published either way. The courts are outdoor asphalt with no lighting on record, in a park the City associates with ice skating in winter, so draw your own conclusion. We are not going to state one as a fact.
Not stated. Tenney Park's three courts are the only ones in Madison the City marks as lighted.

slots.description: Five indoor courts across two gyms: Blue Gym has two and Green Gym three, each 20ft by 44ft. They were the first pickleball courts in this entire directory that could be reserved in advance. The centre stands inside Warner Park on Madison's north side and was expanded to include, in the City's words, "two gymnasiums, a fully equipped fitness center, pickleball courts, flexible studio space, atrium and dry and wet craft rooms". It is published separately from Warner Park's three outdoor courts because the City runs it as a separate facility with its own rules, its own cost and its own booking system.
slots.getting_there: 2930 N. Sherman Ave., Madison, WI 53704, the same address as Warner Park, matched by the Census geocoder to Madison city, Dane County. If you are meeting someone here, be specific about which you mean: the outdoor courts and the recreation center share a street number and nothing else. The City publishes no parking guidance for either.
slots.what_to_expect: Book first. The City runs reservations through its WebTrac account system and asks that you confirm household members on the account before booking. To play you need an active WPCRC ID card and either a Fitness Center/Pickleball membership or a Daily Admission. Annual and six-month memberships and 20-visit passes are available, and all of them include the fitness centre as well as the courts. Wear non-marking rubber-soled shoes; the City asks for them explicitly to protect the gym floors. Neither the membership nor the daily admission price appears on the page we read, so confirm the cost before travelling.

faqs.q: Can I really book a court?
faqs.a: Yes, and this was the first venue on this entire site where that was true; a handful of others have followed. Reservations run through the City's WebTrac account system; every other court in the directory, across nine cities, is first come, first served.

faqs.q: What is the floor made of?
faqs.a: Not stated. The City states the court dimensions and the shoe requirement but never names the surface, so this venue reads "not stated" where the twenty outdoor ones state asphalt or tile.
Youth aged 12 to 17 must be accompanied by an adult, and children under 12 are not allowed in the fitness centre at any time, per the City's rules for the facility.

slots.description: Eight courts on asphalt, the largest outdoor pickleball count in Madison, in a 160-acre community park on the far east side. The City's line under "Tennis & Pickleball" reads "Courts: 8, asphalt", and the park's own description says what kind of courts they are: "tennis courts with shared pickleball courts". So this is the ordinary Madison arrangement at an unusual scale: eight courts of it, where the city's median venue has two.
slots.getting_there: 7035 Littlemore Dr., Madison, WI 53718, on the far east side in the Door Creek neighbourhood. The City lists five alternate access points for the park: 6901 Bluff Point Drive, 851 Harrington Drive, 7202 Cottage Grove Rd., 625 Highcliff Trail and a point between 533 and 601 Highcliff Trail. That is worth knowing in a park this size. It publishes nothing about parking, here or at any Madison venue.
slots.what_to_expect: Eight shared courts is the most pickleball capacity outdoors anywhere in Madison, and the practical consequence is that this is the venue least likely to have you waiting. The courts are tennis courts striped for pickleball, so the net you play over is a tennis net, which the City notes is about two inches taller than a standard pickleball net. Individuals play first come, first served; leagues and lessons must reserve in advance. Lighting is not stated, and neither are nets.

faqs.q: Why did this park only appear recently?
faqs.a: Because of the address, not the courts. This site will not publish a venue whose street address does not resolve, and the Census address file has no record of 7035 Littlemore Dr. On 4 September 2026 a second resolver was added: OpenStreetMap, consulted only where the Census has nothing and accepted only when it returns the house number asked for. It resolves this address, so eight courts that had been refused now publish.
Asphalt, stated in the same line as the count. Madison is the only city in this directory that publishes a surface for every one of its venues.

faqs.q: What else is in the park?
faqs.a: A great deal: 160 acres with a reservable shelter, a large playground, basketball courts, hiking trails, multipurpose fields, and from winter 2025-26 an ice rink with a staffed pavilion renting skis, skates and snowshoes. A cross-country ski permit is required.

slots.description: Six courts on asphalt on the west side, behind Hilldale Mall, in a 20-acre park. The City's line reads "Courts: 6, asphalt" under "Tennis & Pickleball", and the park description fills in what they are: "six tennis courts, three with lighting". Read the two together and this is six tennis courts striped for pickleball, of which three carry lights. The lighting statement is made about the tennis courts in the park's prose and not in the court line the City uses to mark its lit pickleball venues, so lighting is left unstated here rather than published on an inference.
slots.getting_there: 115 N. Eau Claire Ave., Madison, WI 53705, on the west side behind Hilldale Mall; the City gives 518 North Segoe Road as an alternate address. Like Door Creek, this venue waited on an address, and it publishes here from 4 September 2026. The county and postcode come from OpenStreetMap rather than the Census.
slots.what_to_expect: Six shared courts, recently rebuilt on the west side, first come and first served for individuals; leagues and lessons reserve in advance. The net is a tennis net, taller than a pickleball net by the City's own account. Three of the park's six tennis courts have lighting according to the park description, so evening play may be possible, but the City does not say it about the pickleball courts in the line where it says it elsewhere. Treat that as the park's own words rather than as a stated fact on this page.

faqs.a: The west courts were. The City's page carries the note "Update October 20, 2025: West court construction is substantially completed and courts are open for play!", the only recent construction statement Madison makes about any of its court surfaces.

faqs.q: Why did this park only appear recently?
faqs.a: The Census address file has no record of 115 N. Eau Claire Ave., and this site will not publish a venue whose address does not resolve. On 4 September 2026 it added OpenStreetMap as a second resolver, consulted only where the Census has nothing and accepted only at house-number level. It resolves this one.

faqs.q: What else is in the park?
faqs.a: 20 acres behind Hilldale Mall with a large reservable shelter, a climbing-net playground, a free disc golf basket, a concrete ping pong table and checkers table, a community garden, and the Jeff Erlanger accessible playground and sprayground, which opened in 2025.
